routeSelection.route: Ordinary full-time 180-EC Theology bachelor, first-listed 15-EC thematic module and 30 EC free space
routeSelection.basis: The target is the ordinary Theology bachelor, not the separate shortened programme or master. The adopted OER allows a choice of one required thematic module in year three; the first-listed Worldviews, Nature and Climate module is selected independently of UCR fit. The 30-EC genuinely free space remains unspecified; full-time pacing is used to display the coherent 60+60+60 academic route.

exception.reason: UCR offers real philosophical, literary, archaeological, legal and environmental contributions to questions of meaning, ethics and public life. Neither proposed programme sustains the biblical languages and exegesis, Christian doctrines/history, liturgy, pastoral theology and theological research that define Theology. Myth and art with religious themes are not biblical interpretation; general ethics is not theological ethics; climate science and engineering do not supply religious ecology. Coherence and adjacent interests do not establish a sufficiently close complete UCR response.

audience.programmeDescription: Radboud Theology studies Christian texts, beliefs, history and religious practices. Biblical languages and interpretation connect with systematic and practical theology, ethics, empirical research and contemporary social questions.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers useful philosophy, literary study, religious heritage and environmental inquiry. These contributions do not build the sustained biblical, doctrinal and practical theological study at the centre of this degree. We therefore show Radboud’s curriculum without presenting a UCR programme as a sufficiently close alternative.

curriculum.routeLabel: Ordinary full-time Theology bachelor; Worldviews, Nature and Climate module
curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC framework includes 135 EC of required study, one complete 15 EC module and 30 EC of free choice. The selected module has three 5 EC courses. Liturgy is compulsory. Hebrew and Greek develop in two stages; biblical interpretation has its own preparation requirements. Research includes a supervised project and a 10 EC individual final work. RADAr-NL carries no credits; an equivalent university test can support exemption. The usual first-year study-advice threshold is 44 EC. External electives and internships need applicable approval; professional careers may require further qualifications.
